name: withdrawn

relevance.justification: Covers drugs/compounds (core MyChem.info entity) with structured pharmacovigilance annotations: withdrawal reason/toxicity class, withdrawal country list, first/last withdrawn year, first approval year, LD50 estimate, ATC classification, mechanism-of-action predictions (ChEMBL-derived), and FAERS-based adverse event context. Directly aligned with BioThings drug/chemical sphere.

novelty.justification: MyChem.info already ingests SIDER (side effects) and AEOLUS (aggregated FAERS adverse-event counts), so raw adverse-event overlap exists. However, Withdrawn 2.0 contributes curated, drug-withdrawal-specific structured fields not present in any existing BioThings source: toxicity class (hepatic/cardiovascular/hematological/neurological/etc, ProTox-II-derived), predicted LD50, explicit withdrawal country list (ISO3 codes), first/last-withdrawn year, first-approval year, dataset/provenance flag (Safety Withdrawal / EMA / DrugBank Withdrawn / eDrug3D discontinued), and CTD cross-reference ID. No existing BioThings source models 'why and where a drug was withdrawn' as a first-class structured record.

openness.justification: Bulk CSV (`withdrawns.csv`, ~1.65MB, 647 rows) is directly downloadable with no login, API key, or paywall, confirmed via a live HTTP GET (200 OK, content-type: text/csv). No explicit license/terms-of-use statement was found anywhere on the datasource site (homepage, FAQ, contact page) -- this is a minor openness/attribution risk, not a hard blocker, since the data is unrestricted free download for a public academic resource. The underlying NAR article itself is published under CC BY-NC 4.0.

evidence.scope: Curated registry of drugs withdrawn or discontinued in at least one country, integrating pharmacovigilance data (FDA FAERS through June 2023), ChEMBL 29-derived mechanism-of-action/target predictions, KEGG disease-pathway enrichment, and ATC classification, to support adverse-drug-reaction analysis and drug-repositioning research.
evidence.overlap: Overlaps at the compound-identity level with PubChem/ChEMBL/DrugBank/UniChem (already in MyChem.info) and at the adverse-event level with SIDER and AEOLUS (also already in MyChem.info). Withdrawal-specific curation (reason/class, country, dates, LD50) is not duplicated elsewhere in BioThings.

license.name: Not explicitly stated on datasource site (assumed CC BY-NC 4.0, matching the parent NAR article's license)
restrictions: No license/terms-of-use page found on bioinformatics.charite.de/withdrawn_3; assumption carried forward from the NAR publication's stated license, flag for manual confirmation

api_info.record_coverage: No public REST/GraphQL API documented; homepage, FAQ, and contact pages contain no API references. Access is via the web search UI or the bulk CSV download in the FAQ.

risks: No explicit license/terms-of-use statement on the datasource site itself -- assumed CC BY-NC 4.0 from the parent NAR article; should be confirmed with the maintainers before production redistribution.

Site record count (647, live) differs from the paper's abstract framing as an 'update' without a stated total -- treated as a MISMATCH/growth, not an error (paper published Jan 2024; site has grown since).

11 of 647 rows (withdrawnID values DB00052, DB00055, DB00095, DB00111, DB06692, DB11597, DB01038, DB01079, w93, w214, w258) have no usable InChIKey (empty or whitespace-only) and cannot be merged into MyChem.info by structure; these are skipped by the parser, yielding 636 documents.
molfile column contains large embedded 2D-structure blocks (OpenBabel-generated, all-zero coordinates) with no real value beyond what SMILES/InChI already provide -- excluded from parsed output.
